lots.what_it_is: Royal Doulton bone china figurine 'Delight' HN1772 (Leslie Harradine model, made about 1936 to 1967), girl in pink crinoline dress on a black square base.
lots.guide_summary: No same-item evidence survives: nothing sold, unsold or asking for Delight HN1772 was found. As context only (not a guide range), 30 single Royal Doulton lady figures sold at Gowans, Hobart between Sept 2025 and June 2026 for $2 to $100 hammer, mostly $35 to $85 (I re-pulled the API and confirmed the researcher's figures for lots 391998, 388678, 398395, 411403, 398393, 409815, 411408, 395163). All AUD, no rate needed.
lots.working: No SOLD entry for the same model survives, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For reference only: if a Delight sold like the typical Gowans Doulton lady (about $45 to $85 hammer), keep would be about $45/1.22 = $36, rounded down to $35, but that is not same-item evidence and is not a bid limit.
lots.confidence_reason: Mark read clearly in the photo, but there is no same-item SOLD evidence; the WebSearch budget was used up (refused on every attempt), Invaluable search is client-side and returned no data, and the Grays search page had no Delight lots.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped all 7 researcher SOLD entries (Gowans lots 391998 Pretty Ladies $100, 388678 The Cobbler $100, 398395 Angela $85, 411403 Sweet Anne $70, 398393 Sarah $65, 409815 Elaine $45, 395163 Charlotte $10). Prices, dates and kinds were correct (API re-checked, page opened), but none is the Delight HN1772 model, so they are category guides, not the same item. Used only as context in guide_summary.
lots.key_photo_findings: Base enlarged: green printed lion-and-crown 'Royal Doulton England Bone China Made in England' backstamp, title '"Delight"', and painted 'HN 1772' with 'Potd' alongside. Red felt-type circular patch over the base hole. Front shows a full figure with no obvious breaks to hands, head or skirt edges at this resolution. Some grime around the base rim. No copyright date or registration number visible, which suits an earlier production run.
lots.condition: Looks complete and undamaged in two photos, but hairline cracks, restoration to the outstretched hands and fingers, or crazing cannot be ruled out from the photos.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you check the hands, fingers, bonnet ribbon and skirt edges for chips, restoration or hairline cracks, and say whether there is any crazing?

lots.what_it_is: Set of three small graphite (pencil) studies on paper, each about 5 x 5 cm (as written on the back), mounted on small white stretched canvases, by Launceston artist Ryllton Viney, dated 2023; one reverse inscribed 'Study for a Painting (Earthworks 3)'.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing found: no sold, unsold or asking evidence for Ryllton Viney. Gowans API searches for 'viney' returned only wine lots. WebSearch was refused (session budget used up) and the Invaluable search page carries no results in its HTML. No rate needed.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence of any kind, so both maximums are 0.
lots.confidence_reason: Signature and inscription read on one reverse, but there is no price evidence at all; the other two reverses are not shown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Front: three small sketches of curved dome or shed-like 'earthworks' structures, each image about 5 cm square in a wide white canvas surround. Reverse of one: 'Ryllton Viney. 2023. Study for a Painting (Earthworks 3), Pencil on Paper Mounted on Canvas. 5 cm (H) x 5 cm (W)'. Only one back is photographed, so the other two are unconfirmed as signed.
lots.condition: Appears clean and recent (2023). Canvas edges look fine. Two reverses unseen.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are all three studies signed and inscribed on the back by Ryllton Viney, and are they sold as one lot?

lots.what_it_is: Two round hand-painted portrait miniatures of 18th century style ladies (watercolour or gouache, probably late 19th or early 20th century Continental decorative work), in gilt-metal Louis XVI style strut easel frames, one with laurel-wreath crest, the other with ribbon-bow crest, so not a true matched pair.

sold.date: listed 2026-03-01, sold about a week later
sold.note: Kind SOLD. AUD, rate 1.0. same_item: close. '2 MINIATURE PORTRAITS IN ORNATE BRASS FRAMES'. Page opened (API JSON) and photo viewed: two small brass wirework easel frames holding what look like printed or sepia portraits, not hand-painted. Ours are hand-painted with better cast frames but faded and abraded. Hammer only, premium extra.

sold.date: listed 2025-12-01, sold about a week later
sold.note: Kind SOLD. AUD, rate 1.0. same_item: close. 'PAIR OF MINIATURE PORTRAITS IN BONE FRAME - FRAMED'. Page opened (API JSON) and photo viewed: two oval 18th century style lady portraits in a bone or ivorine panel inside a gilt wall frame. Similar subjects, different presentation (one wall frame rather than two easel frames), seemingly better condition. Hammer only.

lots.guide_summary: Two close SOLD results at Gowans, Hobart: $130 and $190 hammer (AUD, rate 1.0), both pairs of small portrait miniatures but not the same item. No unsold or asking evidence. Guide $130 to $190, all sold, all close rather than same-item.
lots.working: Both surviving SOLD results are close but not the same item in similar condition (one is printed portraits in wirework frames, the other a single wall-framed panel), so the rule gives keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For reference only: had the $130 been accepted, keep = 130/1.22 = 106.6, rounded down to $105; flip = (130 less about 15% fees and $15 postage = $95.50)/2.44 = 39.1, rounded down to $35. Not used as limits.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark or signature to read, condition is poor, and evidence is close comparables only; WebSearch budget was used up so no Armitage, Invaluable or dealer results were checked.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped Gowans 378704 ($270, '2 Victorian miniature portraits in gilt frames': photo shows a gentleman portrait in a large oval frame plus a Madonna roundel, different item). Dropped Gowans 409975 ($185, 'Gilt framed miniature portrait': photo shows a single porcelain-style plaque in a large carved giltwood frame, different item). Dropped Gowans 382178 ($120, single Victorian miniature, photo not compared, single not pair). All prices and dates as claimed when re-checked in the API.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged faces: brushwork visible, so hand-painted rather than printed, fairly naive quality. Left: lady with powdered hair holding a bow or quill, colours reasonable. Right: lady with blue flower headdress, heavily faded and washed out, possibly damp-affected. Frames: cast gilt-metal with beaded and leaf borders, different crests (wreath with leaves, and ribbon bow). Backs: one has woven fabric backing, the other torn backing paper exposing the board; wire struts present, gilding worn.
lots.condition: Poor to fair: right portrait badly faded, both glasses dull, one backing torn, gilding worn. Struts intact.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are the portraits painted on ivory, card or paper, are the glasses intact, and is there any signature behind the frames?
